title: First Presbyterian Church gets its Gothic front, tower and spire
items: The 1904 First Presbyterian Church at Indiana Avenue and 21st Street now looks like its 1887 photograph. The front has its rose windows, pointed lancets and a gabled stone porch. A stone coping with a cross runs up the gable, and the tower has its pointed door, a louvred belfry, stepped buttresses with pinnacles, and four gablets. The broad slate spire has its band of small dormers and a finial with a vane.
Each window, course and height is measured off the photograph. The 21st Street side is still plain; a second photograph in the same 1913 book shows it, and that side is next.
